eligibility: An alternative first modern-algebra curriculum for students and future teachers, using historical attempts at Fermat's theorem to organize the technical learning sequence.
reason: The MAA publisher review explicitly evaluates its suitability as a course text and explains the authors' proposed syllabus reform. The historical frame serves instruction.

eligibility: Granville's expanded introductory number-theory course contains induction, the Euclidean algorithm, congruences and progressively advanced material with chapter homework, hints and technical appendices.
reason: The author's own contents and the specialist review establish a teaching text, despite unusually rich motivation and optional exploration.

eligibility: An undergraduate topic-course or self-study text on p-adic arithmetic, topology, analysis and functions, with many exercises and solutions.
reason: Comparisons with real analysis support technical learning; the stated course structure meets H2.

eligibility: A university textbook developing p-adic fields, analysis and extensions through hundreds of exercises; the newer edition also teaches software computation.
reason: Its beginner accessibility and opportunities for exploration do not change the technical training purpose.

eligibility: A mathematical competition-preparation problem collection whose chapters introduce background, demonstrate solved problems and supply practice problems.
reason: The main structure develops problem-solving skill. This is distinct from the differently authored Proofs from THE BOOK.

eligibility: The publisher identifies a solutions volume for the first twelve chapters of Problems from the Book, with additional exposition intended to improve competition and mathematical problem-solving skills.
reason: The stated main objective is technical solutions and skill development, even though the explanations reach current research.

eligibility: A detailed development of polynomial and field theory, computation of Galois groups and applications, addressed to students and professional algebraists, with examples and exercises shaped by undergraduate teaching.
reason: Historical notes and novel applications enrich a technical textbook/reference and do not replace its dominant purpose.

title: Change and Variations: A History of Differential Equations to 1900
eligibility: A historical account explicitly built as a third-year university course, with numerous historical and mathematical exercises, original-source study and extensive guidance on writing student essays.
reason: This is not excluded merely because it is difficult history: the publisher documents a sustained course-study and historical-method training structure that triggers H2.

eligibility: A beginning-undergraduate text that develops algebraic and geometric tools, teaches proof construction and provides the foundations for implementing elliptic-curve cryptography.
reason: The publisher explicitly identifies mathematical skill development and specialist method application as primary purposes.
